Gameplay is more or less the same as in Sniper Elite 5, although with more bugs, which I doubt will ever be fixed. One thing I hate is that the movement of enemies is unrealistically jerky, they twitch all over the place while walking on the stairs, or getting into cover.

It's basically a DLC to Sniper Elite 5. It *should've* been a DLC to Sniper Elite 5, something like Phantom Liberty was for CP2077. That's not to say it's bad, it's just not worth the price of a full game, because it's essentially the same game with new maps, some new weapons, and a different protag. (one who is, unfortunately, just as overly-verbose as Karl -- but now with 200% more british accent for you anglophiles.)

Having said that, they understood much better with Resistance how the maps should be fun to invade on, especially that the first map in the game you can invade on, Dead Drop, is *much* better than Atlantic Wall, the first mission in SE5. I bring this up because, normally, when you go to invade someone else's game, it is far more likely you end up on the first couple missions than the last couple. Atlantic Wall was honestly quite boring to invade people on after the first few times, you could fairly easily guess where someone was based on where it spawned you and what you could see in your immediate vicinity. For instance, radar's blown up and you spawned at the mouth of the tunnel by it? Oh, they're probably coming down that tunnel in the next few seconds, crap a mine in the stairs or camp the tunnel exit, ez win.

Dead Drop is *much* better designed, with more vantage points for long-range duels, more close quarters areas, and an entire underground tunnel network that allows players and invaders alike to move without being exposed. It's also much less on-rails, sure, players *could* go to other objectives than the radar in Atlantic Wall, but it very much encouraged you to go there first, and invasions would always start after you'd completed the first objective. In Dead Drop, the map isn't as large, but it's *much* more dense, and with the tunnel system it's fairly easy to go across the entire map without seeing or being seen by an enemy, meaning it's more likely players will complete objectives in a different order, adding to the challenge of figuring out where they are for the invader.

The other maps, as well, are all much better setpieces for both long range and close quarters encounters than the maps in SE5. SE5 always felt like it was trying too hard to be pretty, but not fun -- it avoided giving you super good vantage points, just sort of okay-ish ones with trees or buildings blocking you in from seeing "too much". This was another big problem with Atlantic Wall, it was huge, took forever to run across, and yet the few high points you could get to really didn't have much to see because of ♥♥♥♥ always being in the way. Here, the maps are pretty *and* fun, and it always provides you enough ability to both get an amazing vantage point, while still very much leaving the door open for someone to sneak around your field of view and get the drop on you. Devil's Cauldron is dark and rainy and hard to see on, and it compensates for this by giving you absolute dominance over huge swathes of the map from multiple high vantage points -- you just have to look really hard. Assault on Fort Rouge is huge and well-lit with equally commanding vantage points, but it's also full of bombed-out ruins with many nooks and crannies to hide in. Sure, there are still sightlines blocked off by trees and buildings, but it's not overdone nearly as much as it was in SE5. There's *just enough* for players to maneuver around and be sneaky, without being so much as to be annoying.

I could go on, but in so many words, if you have SE5 already, just wait for a sale. If you have neither and want to try out invasion mode, get Resistance.

[Introduction]

Sniper Elite: Resistance is the latest installment in the long-running Sniper Elite franchise. While many fans were excited about the game’s release, it quickly became apparent that this iteration offers little to no innovation over its predecessor, Sniper Elite 5. In this review, I’ll break down the various aspects of the game, from its campaign to multiplayer experience, and discuss whether it’s worth the price tag.

[Campaign – More of the Same, but Worse]

The campaign in Sniper Elite: Resistance feels like a reskin of Sniper Elite 5, with minimal changes in gameplay, mission design, or mechanics. While the core sniping mechanics remain solid, two of the available campaigns are outright disappointing, offering nothing but uninspired level designs and reused assets. For a full-priced title, the expectation was for fresh content, new mechanics, and engaging narratives. Instead, the game feels like a repackaged version of SE5, which should have been released as a DLC rather than a standalone title.

[Denuvo – A Non-Issue with Bigger Problems]

Despite the presence of Denuvo anti-cheat software, it appears to be ineffective in curbing cheaters. Multiplayer lobbies are already plagued with unfair play, making competitive modes frustrating for legitimate players. This raises serious concerns about the developer’s commitment to maintaining fair gameplay.

[Axis Invasion – A Copy-Paste Experience]

One of the defining features of Sniper Elite 5, Axis Invasion, makes a return here, but in an almost identical form. No new mechanics, no improved balancing, and no additional depth have been added. If you’ve played Axis Invasion in SE5, you’ve already experienced everything Resistance has to offer in this mode.

[Multiplayer Maps – Severely Lacking Content]

The multiplayer experience in Sniper Elite: Resistance is incredibly limited due to a severe lack of maps:

•	Team Deathmatch – Only three maps are available, drastically reducing variety and replayability.
•	No Cross – Limited to a single map, which quickly becomes stale for returning players.

For a game that demands a premium price, this level of content restriction is unacceptable. Multiplayer should have been expanded with fresh maps, innovative modes, and improved balancing, but instead, it feels like an afterthought.

[Early Access Gimmick – A Cash Grab]

The early access model used for this game was nothing more than a clever marketing strategy at best and an outright scam at worst. Rather than investing in proper game testers, the developers essentially charged players to test the game for them. While early access can sometimes be a beneficial model, in this case, it only served to exploit paying customers.

[Bugs – A Lack of Quality Control]

As a software developer, I generally overlook minor bugs, understanding that no game is perfect at launch. However, Sniper Elite: Resistance suffers from numerous glaring issues that should have been caught in even the most basic testing phases. The sheer volume of bugs makes it evident that the game was rushed out without adequate QA, further diminishing its already limited appeal.

[Final Verdict – Buy or Wait?]

If you’re considering picking up Sniper Elite: Resistance, ask yourself this: Is it worth spending $60–$80 for what is essentially a rebranded version of SE5 with minimal additions? If you can find the game for under $30, it might be worth a try, especially if you’re a hardcore fan of the series. Otherwise, wait for a sale or skip it altogether.

[Final Score: 2/10] – A disappointing, recycled experience that fails to justify its price.

[Disclaimer on Playtime]

100+ hours ≠ quality. 

A note on playtime, since it often comes up: a significant portion of my hours comes from playing with friends, not from my personal recommendation of the game. Social play does not reflect my assessment of content quality, innovation, or value for money. When playing solo, I still return to Sniper Elite 4, which I consider the strongest entry in the franchise. 

I paid for it, so I played it. Doesn't mean it's good. Just means I wanted to get my money’s worth. Friends are playing, so I join in. Gaming is social, but that doesn’t fix the game’s flaws.Some of that was me trying to enjoy it, dealing with bugs, or just waiting for something new. 

Developers don’t ‘crumble’ from criticism; they crumble when they stop innovating. Reusing SE5’s mechanics without real improvements makes this feel like overpriced DLC, not a new game. If you’re okay with that, cool. But don’t dismiss valid critiques just because ‘I played it a lot.’

TLDR: If I had a choice, I would uninstall it.

[h1] Sniper Elite: Resistance is more of the same, which is both it's strength and it's greatest hinderance. [/h1]

[h2] Story: [/h2]
You know what WW2 was, right? Then you know the story. Nazis are the bad guys, you're the good guy. You're tasked with tracking and eliminating a secret Nazi chemical weapon which threatens the D-Day landing.
This game is the first in the series to follow Harry Hawker, who you may recognize as the co-op character from previous Sniper Elite games. While it's unclear whether he's a full time-replacement for Karl Fairburne going forward, he's likable enough. He's a little more sassy and snarky, and lacks the stoic gravely voice of Fairburne (as played by Tom Clarke Hill), but I never found him annoying. If anything, he came off as a little flat and one-dimensional, but I'm okay with a game about creating exit wounds in fascist skulls being light on character development.

[h2] Gameplay: [/h2]
A lot of people have stated their concerns that this feels like an extended DLC for Sniper Elite 5, and while I totally agree, I also don't think that's necessarily a bad thing. There are new weapons and new maps, but everything else just feels like boilerplate Sniper Elite. There are no new game mechanics or new enemy types, and while it feels like the game is starting to take some notes from the Hitman series, the examples I could give are too few and far between to be meaningful. The gunplay is still satisfying, and the controls are tight and responsive enough that I still had a lot of fun with it. By far my biggest gripe about this game is the number of bugs I experienced during my 12 hour campaign stint with the game. Enemies would occasionally spot me through walls or hedges, the AI would act completely nonsensically (enemies on the other side of the map would become cautious for no apparent reason), and I would regularly experience issues with getting caught in level geometry. One particularly frustrating bug involved a Nazi which had fallen through a staircase and continue to spot me and shoot at me from inside the level geometry, despite me not being able to shoot back at them. I don't think the game needs to reinvent the wheel every new entry, but I think a little innovation in the gameplay (and a big step up in quality control) could go a long way in helping players feel like they weren't paying $50 for an extended DLC.

[h2] Visuals/Audio: [/h2]
The game looks and plays great both on Steam Deck and Desktop. On Steam Deck, medium settings got me a pretty solid 60fps, but you could probably squeeze a little more fidelity out of the game if you don't mind 30-40fps. Personally, I preferred playing it on my computer. This graphics are crisp and clear, and the wide open vistas you usually start out in are incredible in an ultrawide aspect ratio with the FOV pulled back a bit.
As far as the audio is concerned, and I could be mistaken, but they could have very well dragged and dropped the sound effects and music from Sniper Elite 5 and I'd have no idea. There is nothing notable about the audio that grabbed my attention. The sound mask from generators is the same. The sounds of the bullet time camera are the same. I wouldn't be surprised if the voice lines of the German soldiers is the same. It sounds good as ever, but there's nothing to write home about.

[h3] Personal thoughts: [/h3]
If ain't broke, don't fix it. Unfortunately, I think a good number of bugs in this game need to be fixed. If you liked Sniper Elite 5, you'll probably like this game. It doesn't do anything different, which begs the question "Is it worth the asking price of $50?" That's for you to decide. I got it for $35 at launch, and I feel like that was a pretty fair price. Overall, I enjoyed my time with this one, which is why I'm recommending it, but I do hope that we see a little bit of innovation in the next game while still staying true to the core mechanics that make the Sniper Elite series so fun to play.

This review assumes you're familiar with and play and enjoy the Sniper Elite series as a whole, or it won't make a huge amount of sense.

First off, what are you getting for your bucks? TLDR: You're getting a full-priced expansion for Sniper Elite 5.

Is that a bad thing? Yes and no. If I'm paying full price for a game, then I don't expect it to be littered with bugs and be a step backward from the previous release, which this does feel like. You're getting a handful of missions which range in size and scope from a quick hour through to a huge, daunting scale. Not much different from SE5. Some of the maps are a lot darker - taking place often at night - but nowhere near the complexity and incredible design of Sniper Elite 4 (which I take to be the pinnacle of the series). I found more than a few times my feet got stuck on doors and floors, especially at the top of stairs. 

There's new ammo types in explosive and other assorted slightly less interesting variants, some new trooper types and turrets. Hawker though is a great addition to the franchise; he looks like Danny Dyer, talks like Jason Statham and shoots like Karl Fairburn. Great combo and a good addition.

If you liked SE5 then you'll like this, although it really does need polish. There's the odd acknowledged bug - the poison in one mission where you just can't get the horrid nazi to drink - and the aforementioned glitching on stairs. The roughest level by far, however, is in the return of the "kill Hitler" mission. Not only did I have to save and reload several times to be able to interact with the various methods by which you can kill him (no spoilers here but they've really gone to town and put loads in) but I couldn't get Hitler to move at all so had to settle for a bullet in the plums. At one point I fell through the map. Several times I got stuck on stairs. I honestly and frankly expect better.

Having put all of this out there, having said all that, would I recommend it? If you're a fan of the series then yes, absolutely, it's a no-brainer. It builds on the other games and adds extra missions as though it were DLC to SE5. But honestly I really miss the map design and story of SE4 - the architecture of those maps was just sublime.

If this were speed dating then I'd be happy to date SE5 and SER but honestly I'd be thinking about SE4 while doing it.

So, yeah, this really is just an extension of Sniper Elite 5.  The game is almost exactly the same, but with different missions, and huge maps.  The voice acting is "meh."  To be honest, I thought the storyline was not very well written, and was again "meh," but I do enjoy the game.  I didn't care for mechanic where you have to find weapons tables in each mission in order to get new equipment/accessories.  Those should come available as you gain XP IMO.  Overall, if you're a fan of the Sniper Elite series, then you'll be fairly happy, but I'd wait until the it goes on sale.  I just don't think it merits being called a "stand alone" release, and is more of DLC for SE5.
